title: Audit event sampling and rehydration protocol for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML-linked admin actions increase, audit log volume is growing rapidly. Storing full, verbatim pre/post payloads for every admin mutation (policy edits, role assignments, SSO mappings) is unsustainable for cost and throughput. We need a structure that lets us retain high-fidelity change records for critical actions while sampling lower-value events, and a reliable rehydration mechanism to reconstruct full context when requested (for investigations, compliance, or customer support).

This ticket defines a sampling + rehydration protocol and event envelope for RBAC v2 admin/audit events. Goals: reduce storage and ingestion costs, preserve forensic capability on demand, keep actor/target identity linkage intact (including SSO subject mapping), and make sampling decisions auditable and reversible. This should interoperate with existing audit consumers (security dashboards, legal exports, incident analysis pipeline).
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact audit envelope schema that supports both full and sampled events and includes rehydration metadata.
Sampling policy DSL and configuration: per-action-type, per-customer-tier, per-actor-risk-score, and timebound sampling windows.
Implement server-side sampling with deterministic hashing to allow stable sampling at the shard level and reproducible replays.
Add rehydration API that, given an event id and proof-of-authorization, returns the full pre/post payload or a signed pointer to archival store.
Migration plan and feature-flagged rollout with telemetry to measure storage savings and rehydration latency/availability.
Security review completed for rehydration endpoints and retention controls (KMS, authz) and threat modeling documented.
implementation_notes: Event envelope: top-level fields: event_id, timestamp, event_type, actor{type,id,provider,ssn_hash_hint}, target{type,id,namespace}, action_summary, change_delta (if sampled: compressed-diff-ref), severity, sampling_metadata.

Two payload modes: full (payloads.pre_payload, payloads.post_payload) and sampled (delta_reference + compact_delta_shingles). Full payloads stored in hot retention for 30d then moved to cold archive; sampled events store compact delta + provenance metadata in primary index for 365d.

Diff encoding: use a shallow JSON-Patch-like delta augmented with field provenance (field path -> op -> value-hash) to preserve accountability while keeping size small. Non-deterministic fields (timestamps, nonces, ephemeral tokens) are normalized and not included in deltas.

Sampling rules engine: prioritized rule set evaluated in order: non-sample-exempt actions (policy deletions, privilege escalations) -> actor risk overrides (SAML identity flagged) -> project/customer tier -> deterministic hash(bucket) for steady-state sampling. Rules are configurable via Console and stored as jsonnet rulesets in config-service.
Deterministic sampling: compute hash(event_id || actor.id || target.id) mod 10000 and compare to configured threshold to ensure consistent sampling across retries and replicas.

Rehydration API: endpoint POST /audit/rehydrate with params {event_id, requester_id, purpose, auth_proof}. Returns signed URL to archival blob (time-limited) or the full reconstructed event blob. All accesses logged to audit-access ledger and require authorization scope 'audit:rehydrate'.

Proof-of-authorization: support Service-to-Service JWT with x5c chain OR user-authz via console SSO SAML session. Rehydration requests from Support must include case-id and be tied to a customer-specific authorization policy (consent or legal hold).

Archival: full payloads encrypted with customer KMS key where available; archival pointers include KMS key id and encryption metadata for decryption during rehydration with appropriate key access checks.
Backwards compatibility: the envelope includes 'schema_version' and a migration shim will transform older audit rows into the new envelope for downstream consumers.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (feature flag off): implement envelope write path and sampling engine in a shadow mode that records sampling decisions but still stores full payloads; validate metrics for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (flag on for low-risk customers): enable sampling for low-tier projects at 10% baseline; monitor rehydration request volume and missed-data incidents.

Phase 3 (incremental rollout): increase sampling coverage and enable cold-archival pointer promotion for sampled events; run two-week audits on sampled vs full event fidelity for random sample of events.
Phase 4: enable customer KMS-backed archival and opt-in controls in Console; deprecate legacy full-storage for non-exempt actions after 90 days of successful rollout.
Rollback plan: toggle sampling thresholds to 0% and rehydrate recently sampled events from archived full copies while investigation completes.
monitoring_and_alerts: Metrics: sampled_event_ratio by action_type, rehydration_success_rate, rehydration_latency P50/P95/P99, archive_fetch_errors, storage_bytes_saved.
Alerts: rehydration_success_rate < 99% over 15m for > 10 events -> P1 oncall; archive_fetch_errors spike -> P0 incident if > 1% of requests fail; sampling_rule_misfires -> P2.
Dashboards: 'Audit Sampling Health' with real-time sampling ratio, per-customer variance, and recent rehydration sessions with audit-access logs.
